sources.title: Narasimhan and colleagues, formation of South and Central Asian populations
sources.note: Genome-wide data from Iran, Turan, the steppe and South Asia, with radiocarbon context and mixture models.

sources.title: Guarino-Vignon and colleagues, Bronze to Iron Age population dynamics in Uzbekistan
sources.note: Ancient genomes show Bronze Age continuity, later mixture and limits of simple population-replacement stories.

sources.title: Martinez and colleagues, Bronze Age individual from Ulug Depe
sources.note: One Ulug Depe genome placed with the BMAC cluster, illustrating both continuity and sample-size limits.

sources.title: Spengler and colleagues, early agriculture among Central Eurasian mobile pastoralists
sources.note: Direct plant remains from Ojakly, Tasbas and other camps document wheat, barley, millet, peas and mobility.

sources.title: Hermes and colleagues, early integration of pastoralism and millet cultivation
sources.note: Animal genetics and isotopes connect sheep, goat, cattle management with millet fodder and cultivation.

sources.title: Taylor and colleagues, early pastoral economies in the Alay Valley
sources.note: ZooMS, ancient DNA and radiocarbon dating identify sheep-centered herding with cattle, goats and possible crops.

sources.title: Motuzaite Matuzeviciute and colleagues, high-elevation agriculture in the central Tien Shan
sources.note: Directly dated wheat and barley demonstrate highland cultivation and the small scale of current samples.

sources.title: Spengler and colleagues, archaeobotany of the Pamirs and Fergana foothills
sources.note: Plant remains reveal varied high-elevation agropastoral strategies and continuing regional evidence gaps.

sources.title: Miehe and colleagues, long-term agropastoral landscapes in Inner Asian mountains
sources.note: Pollen, charcoal and other proxies reconstruct gradual human shaping of mountain grasslands and forests.

sources.title: Li and colleagues, early mounted pastoralists in the Kunlun Mountains
sources.note: Radiocarbon-dated burials, houses, crops, animals and riding equipment localize early first-millennium lifeways.

sources.title: Wilkin and colleagues, five thousand years of Eastern Steppe dairying
sources.note: Dental-calculus proteins document ruminant milk and later horse milk with strong chronological and geographic controls.

sources.title: Zhang and colleagues, genomic origins of Bronze Age Tarim Basin mummies
sources.note: Genome-wide data reveal a distinctive Tarim population and reject automatic equations among ancestry, material culture and language.

sources.title: Librado and colleagues, origins and spread of domestic horses
sources.note: Ancient horse genomes track the rapid second-millennium spread of DOM2 horses without identifying their riders languages.

sources.title: UNESCO, State Historical and Cultural Park Ancient Merv
sources.note: Institutional synthesis of Bronze and Iron Age oasis centers, changing river courses and long urban continuity.

sources.title: Turkmenistan and UNESCO, Ancient Merv nomination dossier
sources.note: Detailed site, settlement, canal, mudbrick and landscape documentation for the Murghab oasis.

sources.title: UNESCO History of Civilizations of Central Asia, Volume I
sources.note: Scholarly synthesis of Bronze and Iron Age settlements, pastoralism, farming, burials, crafts and chronology.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Iranica, pre-Islamic archaeology of Central Asia
sources.note: Reference synthesis of Yaz pottery, oasis settlements, fortifications, horses and competing migration interpretations.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Iranica, iron in eastern Iran
sources.note: Chronology and archaeological contexts for iron knives, sickles, needles, weapons and continuing bronze use.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Iranica, pre-Islamic Bactria
sources.note: Geographic and archaeological distinction between Bactrian river oases, later political names and nomadic neighbors.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Iranica, Iranian languages in Central Asia
sources.note: States the lack of indisputable language evidence before the first millennium and reviews later regional languages.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Iranica, Iranian languages and scripts
sources.note: Distinguishes reconstructed Proto-Iranian, Old Iranian languages, geographic spread and written documentation.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Iranica, Avesta history and contents
sources.note: Explains oral transmission, uncertain dating, later compilation and the absence of an early manuscript sample.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Iranica, pre-Islamic Persian literature
sources.note: Identifies the 519 BCE Bisotun Old Persian version as the first securely dateable Iranian-language text.

sources.title: UNESCO, Bisotun World Heritage property
sources.note: Dates Darius monumental trilingual inscription to 521 to 520 BCE and identifies its Old Persian version.

sources.title: Lhuillier, Bendezu-Sarmiento and Lecomte, Ulug Depe Iron Age overview
sources.note: Excavation synthesis of long stratigraphy, Yaz I and II architecture, pottery and funerary evidence.

sources.title: Tengberg and colleagues, environment and subsistence at Iron Age Ulug Depe
sources.note: Archaeobotanical and archaeozoological results document localized cultivation, herding and environmental use.

sources.title: Dubova and colleagues, polychrome painting from Gonur Depe
sources.note: Excavated satellite settlement documents ovens, kilns, homes, graves, ornaments and rare steppe-related material.

sources.title: Sabori and colleagues, rounded potsherds at Tepeh Ferizi
sources.note: Surface survey and geomorphology reveal a northeastern Iranian settlement, artifacts and post-depositional movement.

sources.title: Berger and colleagues, origin of Bronze Age tin and copper in Central Asia
sources.note: Elemental and isotopic analyses investigate ores, mines, alloys and multi-stage Central Asian metal circulation.

sources.title: Doumani Dupuy and colleagues, textile impressions among Central Eurasian pastoralists
sources.note: Ceramic impressions preserve woven structures and connect textile skill with mobile pastoral communities.

sources.title: Kufterin and Dubova, Late Bronze Age skeletal remains from Gonur Depe
sources.note: Analysis of 920 people reports childhood stress, dental disease, trauma, infection and joint conditions.

sources.title: Kufterin, tumor-like lesions in a Gonur Depe skeleton
sources.note: A single Late Bronze Age skeleton illustrates rare pathology and the limits of individual diagnosis.

sources.title: Wallaert-Petre and colleagues, ceramic learning in household settings
sources.note: Later ethnoarchaeological comparison for observation, practice, mistakes and household craft apprenticeship.

sources.title: Wu, searching for Zoroastrian fire temples in Central Asia
sources.note: Reviews why most scholars reject labeling Bronze Age Gonur and Togolok buildings as Zoroastrian fire temples.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum, Art of the Bronze Age
sources.note: Museum catalogue localizes vessels, seals, ornaments, stones, metals and cross-regional stylistic connections.

sources.title: Baumer and Novak, Urban Cultures of Central Asia
sources.note: Open scholarly volume on houses, towns, graves, children, institutions and settlement change across Central Asia.

sources.title: Austrian Academy of Sciences, Archaeology of Central Asia during the first millennium BCE
sources.note: Scholarly volume contents covering Ulug Depe subsistence, Bactra, Chorasmia and regional Iron Age chronology.

sources.title: Kohl, Central Asia in the Bronze Age: sedentary and nomadic cultures
sources.note: Regional synthesis emphasizes interaction between oasis settlements and mobile groups rather than a hard binary.

sources.title: Ventresca Miller and colleagues, North Central Asia isotopic database
sources.note: Open dataset of human, animal and plant isotopes with geographic, chronological and contextual metadata.

sources.title: Macklin and colleagues, river civilizations of Central Asia
sources.note: Hydrology, dates and irrigation archaeology show why environmental change cannot be reduced to automatic collapse.

sources.title: Shishlina and colleagues, diet in Bronze Age pastoral communities
sources.note: Stable isotopes show regional dietary diversity and caution against imagining pastoral diets as only meat and milk.

sources.title: Akcalı and Lang, dental calculus in archaeology
sources.note: Review explains how mineralized plaque traps food particles, microbes and other evidence, with interpretive limits.

scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.
Agent researched a disjoint batch; integration and structural checks are not independent historical certification.
Imported border coordinates remain unchanged. Historical events and map coverage are distinguished in prose; see batchIdentityNotes for conflicts.

proposedOverrides.summary: Atlas umbrella across eastern Iran, southern Central Asia, Afghanistan and Kashgar, circa 1500 to 500 BCE.

batchIdentityNotes: The exact indexed id and display name are preserved as historical-basemap metadata, not an ancient self-name.
Three exact Polygon snapshots cover the continuous indexed lifetime from 1500 to 500 BCE.
The decoded footprint excludes most of western Iran and reaches east through Central Asia, Afghanistan and Kashgar.
The target is not one Iranian-speaking people, ethnicity, ancestry, archaeological culture, state or uniform pastoral economy.
Archaeological material, ancient DNA, historical linguistics and later written records are kept analytically separate.
Named sites and scientific results remain localized, with later ethnographic or regional comparisons labeled.
No writing sample is supplied because none is securely attributable to the exact umbrella and interval.
The 500 BCE endpoint is an atlas redraw dominated by an Achaemenid label, not one shared fall or disappearance.
Predecessor and successor arrays remain empty because the umbrella is not a historical polity or ethnicity.
